module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 757

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/757](https://www.erdosproblems.com/757)
 - [GyLe95] Gyárfás, András and Lehel, Jenő, Linear sets with five distinct differences among any
    four elements. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B (1995), 108-118.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped Pointwise
open Filter

namespace Erdos757

/-- We say that `c` is admissible if, for any finite set `A` such that every four-element
subset `B` determines at least five positive differences, there exists a Sidon subset `S`
of size at least `c * A.ncard`. The difference condition is equivalent to
`11 ≤ (B - B).ncard`. -/
def IsAdmissible (c : ℝ) : Prop := ∀ {A : Set ℝ}, A.Finite → (∀ B ⊆ A,
  B.ncard = 4 → 11 ≤ (B - B).ncard) → ∃ S ⊆ A, IsSidon S ∧ c * A.ncard ≤ (S.ncard : ℝ)

/-- What is the supremum of the set of admissible numbers? -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_757 {A : Set ℝ} :
    answer(sorry) = sSup {c | IsAdmissible c} := by
  sorry

/-- The supremum is strictly larger than `1 / 2`, which is proved in [GyLe95]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_757.variants.lowerBound {A : Set ℝ} : 1 / (2 : ℝ) < sSup {c | IsAdmissible c} := by
  sorry

/-- In [GyLe95], the authors also prove that the supremum is smaller than `3 / 5`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_757.variants.upperBound {A : Set ℝ} : sSup {c | IsAdmissible c} < 3 / (5 : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos757

findings.description: The docstring incorrectly attributes the strict bound `sSup {c | IsAdmissible c} < 3 / 5` to [GyLe95]. That paper establishes only the non-strict bound c_* ≤ 3/5. The Lean inequality is nevertheless mathematically valid today: Ma–Tang prove c_* ≤ 4/7 < 3/5. Thus this is an attribution error, not a mathematical misformalization or a status issue.
findings.source_evidence: Gyárfás–Lehel, Corollary 2.5, p. 112, bounds the guaranteed Sidon subset size by 3n/5 + 1, yielding c_* ≤ 3/5 (https://users.renyi.hu/~gyarfas/Cikkek/69_linset5.pdf). Ma–Tang, arXiv:2602.23282v2, §1.2, explicitly restate the Gyárfás–Lehel bound as c_* ≤ 3/5 and then prove 9/17 ≤ c_* ≤ 4/7; §5.1 supplies the 14-point upper-bound example.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain the strict inequality but attribute it to Ma–Tang and add a reference to arXiv:2602.23282v2. Alternatively, if this variant is intended specifically to record [GyLe95], change `<` to `≤` and revise the docstring accordingly.

reformulations.difference: The distance-based formulation is expressed using eleven signed differences and the additive `IsSidon` predicate.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a nonempty finite real set B, its difference set is the disjoint union of zero, its positive differences D, and −D. Hence |B−B| = 2|D| + 1, making the thresholds eleven and five equivalent. A four-element B is necessarily nonempty. Over ℝ, uniqueness of positive differences is equivalent to uniqueness of pairwise sums up to interchanging summands, exactly `IsSidon`. The full admissibility-predicate equivalence was proved in `/workspace/review/sidon_equiv.lean`.

reformulations.difference: The source's best constant is represented by the real supremum of all admissible constants.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The admissible set is nonempty because zero is admissible, and bounded above by one by considering a singleton. For each finite input A, a largest Sidon subset exists. Every admissible constant satisfies the corresponding cardinality bound, so their supremum does too; therefore the supremum is itself admissible and is the greatest admissible constant. The empty input is harmless, and the known lower bound ensures positivity. The equivalence between identifying this supremum and identifying the greatest admissible constant was proved in `/workspace/review/scratch.lean`.

review.notes: Checked all four declarations. The source still records problem 757 as open; Ma–Tang improve its bounds rather than determine the constant. No mathematical misformalizations were found. Scratch proofs verified finiteness of all counted sets, safe use of the real supremum, and boundary cases without using sorry-backed results. Additional Lean computations in `/workspace/review/upper_bound_witness.lean` confirmed that Ma–Tang's 14-point example satisfies the condition on all 1001 four-element subsets and has maximum Sidon subset size 8.
